reported_data.population: High-risk BCG-unresponsive NMIBC with carcinoma in situ with or without Ta/T1. The interim disclosure included 35 evaluable participants, with 22 evaluable at six months and 15 at 12 months.
reported_data.efficacy: Complete response at any time was 65.7% (23/35), six-month complete response was 68.2% (15/22), and 12-month complete response was 33.3% (5/15). The Kaplan-Meier estimated probability of maintaining complete response for six months was 71.1%; 5/5 responders maintained response from nine to 12 months, and reinduction converted 8/13 patients to a six-month complete response.
reported_data.safety: Most treatment-related adverse events were grade 1 and transient. There were no grade 3 or greater treatment-related adverse events, no related serious adverse events and no discontinuations due to treatment-related adverse events.
reported_data.follow_up: Landmark follow-up was available through 12 months for 15 patients, but the denominator was still small and the registrational cohort remained open to enrollment.

reported_data.population: High-risk BCG-naïve NMIBC with carcinoma in situ with or without Ta/T1. Enrollment was complete at 31 participants; 29 were evaluable, 27 at six months and 19 at 12 months.
reported_data.efficacy: Complete response at any time was 72.4% (21/29), six-month complete response was 66.7% (18/27), and 12-month complete response was 57.9% (11/19). The Kaplan-Meier estimated probability of maintaining complete response for six months was 73.1%; 11/11 responders maintained response from nine to 12 months, and reinduction converted 4/6 patients to a six-month complete response.
reported_data.safety: Most treatment-related adverse events were grade 1 and transient. There were no grade 3 or greater treatment-related adverse events, no related serious adverse events and no discontinuations due to treatment-related adverse events.
reported_data.follow_up: Landmark follow-up was available through 12 months for 19 patients; the cohort was fully enrolled but longer durability remained immature.

competitor_comparisons.matched_setting: BCG-unresponsive NMIBC with carcinoma in situ with or without papillary tumors in a single-arm registrational cohort.
competitor_comparisons.clinical_comparison: The FDA clinical summary reported an 82% complete response rate among 83 patients, with 51% of responders maintaining response for at least 12 months. TARA-002 showed encouraging six-month activity and a favorable safety profile, but its 12-month landmark denominator was small and its observed 12-month complete-response proportion was lower.
competitor_comparisons.limitations: Cross-trial comparison with different schedules, response adjudication, follow-up maturity and denominators; the TARA-002 cohort remained an interim analysis.

competitor_comparisons.competitor: Sasanlimab plus BCG induction and maintenance in CREST
competitor_comparisons.matched_setting: BCG-naïve high-risk NMIBC after resection; randomized Phase 3 evidence, although the systemic checkpoint-plus-BCG regimen and endpoint differ from intravesical TARA-002.
competitor_comparisons.clinical_comparison: CREST randomized 352 patients to sasanlimab plus BCG induction and maintenance and 351 to BCG alone, with an event-free-survival hazard ratio of 0.68 and estimated 36-month event-free survival of 82.1% versus 74.8%. TARA-002's 57.9% 12-month complete response and clean early tolerability are encouraging, but follow-up and sample size are far less mature.
competitor_comparisons.limitations: Cross-trial comparison across different endpoints, treatment modalities, follow-up horizons and study designs; TARA-002 lacks randomized evidence at this event.

target_assessments.data_quality: Moderate: clinically meaningful six-month activity and a clean tolerability profile in 35 evaluable patients, offset by a small 12-month denominator, declining landmark response and ongoing enrollment.
target_assessments.clinical_interpretation: The six-month response, successful reinduction and lack of severe treatment-related toxicity support a positive revision. The lower 12-month landmark result and stronger mature intravesical competitor benchmark constrain the size and preserve both neutral and modest downside branches.

outcomes.rationale: A 68.2% six-month complete response, reinduction activity and no grade 3 or greater treatment-related toxicity support a meaningful positive adjustment.
The immature 12-month denominator and competitive efficacy bar could leave assumptions unchanged until the registrational cohort matures.
The 33.3% 12-month landmark proportion and stronger mature benchmark create a limited downside branch despite favorable six-month data.
Observed efficacy, tolerability and continuing registrational enrollment do not support suspension.

target_assessments.data_quality: Moderate: a nearly complete cohort with 29 evaluable patients, consistent six- and 12-month complete responses and favorable safety, but still a small nonrandomized dataset.
target_assessments.clinical_interpretation: The 57.9% 12-month complete response and clean safety support a positive revision. The randomized CREST benchmark and the lack of a control arm keep a substantial neutral branch and limit extrapolation.

outcomes.rationale: Consistent six- and 12-month complete responses, reinduction activity and no severe treatment-related toxicity support an upward adjustment.
The nonrandomized 29-patient evidence may not justify a durable assumption change against a mature randomized competitor standard.
A downside interpretation would require later durability or controlled efficacy to disappoint; current data make this below the retention threshold.
The efficacy and safety disclosure does not support suspension.
